title: Object-Oriented Python
subtitle: Understand classes, objects, methods and the foundations of object-oriented programming.
description: Learn how classes and objects work and how object-oriented design can organize larger Python applications.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 9: Object-Oriented Python. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Object-Oriented Python”. The goal is to understand classes, objects, methods and the foundations of object-oriented programming.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
A class or equivalent type can group related state and behavior into one understandable model. An object is an instance of that model, with its own current values.

blocks.title: Sample 1: Object-Oriented Python in practice

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Understand classes, objects, methods and the foundations of object-oriented programming. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: A class has one hundred unrelated methods. What is the likely design problem?
options: It needs more responsibilities.
Its name is too short.
It has too many unrelated responsibilities and should be split.
It should stop being tested.
blocks.explanation: A type with many unrelated jobs is difficult to understand, change, and test.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A type with many unrelated jobs is difficult to understand, change, and test.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A type with many unrelated jobs is difficult to understand, change, and test.

blocks.title: Sample 2: Object-Oriented Python in practice

blocks.text: Application tip: in a real Python project, choose names and structures that reveal the reason the code exists. Do not copy a snippet into a project without checking its assumptions and adapting it to the surrounding code.

blocks.question: A child type must work wherever a parent contract is expected. What matters most?
options: Matching the parent’s color.
Preserving the expected behavior of the contract.
Having the most methods possible.
Using global state instead of parameters.
blocks.explanation: Subtypes should honor the behavior callers expect from the shared abstraction.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Subtypes should honor the behavior callers expect from the shared abstraction.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Subtypes should honor the behavior callers expect from the shared abstraction.

blocks.text: Encapsulation protects an object’s rules. For example, a balance should not become negative simply because any caller can edit an internal field; provide operations that validate changes instead.

blocks.title: Sample 3: Object-Oriented Python in practice

blocks.question: Several values and operations always belong together in a domain model. What design helps?
options: Global variables scattered through every screen.
A focused class/type that groups related data and behavior.
One class with every unrelated feature.
A collection of unlabelled numbers.
blocks.explanation: A cohesive type communicates related state and behavior together.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A cohesive type communicates related state and behavior together.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A cohesive type communicates related state and behavior together.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning

Use inheritance only when one type truly is a specialized form of another. Prefer simple composition when one object merely needs to use another, and keep each type responsible for a small, coherent job.

blocks.title: Sample 4: Object-Oriented Python in practice

blocks.text: Before continuing, explain in your own words how this topic helps solve the dashboard goal: Learn how classes and objects work and how object-oriented design can organize larger Python applications. Try one boundary case, one normal case, and one case that should be rejected or handled differently.

blocks.question: An object must never allow its balance to fall below zero. Which design protects the rule?
options: Allow any caller to rewrite the field.
Document the rule but never check it.
Hide every object method.
Control updates through methods that validate the new balance.
blocks.explanation: Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how state changes.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how state changes.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how state changes.

blocks.question: Two types share a small helper behavior but are not true specializations of one another. What should be considered?
options: Composition or a focused interface instead of forcing inheritance.
An inheritance chain of many levels.
Duplicating the helper in every method.
Making all fields public.
blocks.explanation: Inheritance should represent a genuine “is-a” relationship; composition is often better for using a capability.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Inheritance should represent a genuine “is-a” relationship; composition is often better for using a capability.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Inheritance should represent a genuine “is-a” relationship; composition is often better for using a capability.
